newsitem.title: USA: Uni of Texas approves $4.76 bln budget for 1998.
newsitem.headline: Uni of Texas approves $4.76 bln budget for 1998.

text.p: The University of Texas board of regents approved a budget of $4.76 billion for fiscal 1998, up 6.28 percent from this year, for the system's 15 universities and health science centers, officials said Friday.

Spokesman Monty Jones said the board also updated the system's six-year capital improvements program, adding another $300 million worth of projects to bring the total to $1.8 billion through the year 2003.
The new plan, approved at a meeting Wednesday, envisages a total of 133 construction projects throughout the system.

The increases in the new budget, effective September 1, would mostly pay for faculty merit raises, a $1,200 salary hike for the non-faculty staff and higher utility bills. The current budget is $4.48 billion.
The increased spending will be met with an increase in tuition fees of $2 to $34 per credit hour, as well as higher fees paid at the system's six health centers.
Jones said state appropriations to the system totaled $1.23 billion, up 5.3 percent over the current budget.
The capital improvements plan would be partly funded by $635 million in revenue bonds, and $931 million of institutional funds, gifts and grants.
The rest will come from the system's Permanent University Fund bonds that are backed by endowment funds and equity investments.
The largest recipient will be the system's main campus at Austin with 34 projects at a cost of $478 million, Jones said.
The UT system has total student enrollment of about 145,000 and employs about 68,000 faculty and non-faculty people.
